title: The Holy See
hookLine: the pope's office and the tiny state that protects it

lines: NOT VATICAN CITY, THE HOLY SEE.
cards: When a new ambassador arrives in Rome to represent a country to the pope, the paperwork doesn't say Vatican City. It names something else: the Holy See.
Two names, one small patch of ground beside the Tiber, and they aren't the same thing. One is a state, with walls, gardens, a post office and stamps. The other isn't a place at all.
It's an office, and the state exists to keep it free.

teach.b: Back on day six hundred fifty-three, the Chair of Saint Peter: a feast of Peter's teaching office, not a piece of furniture. See is an old word for a seat, and yesterday you met one: the bishop's chair in the cathedral.
Every bishop has a see. The pope is the bishop of Rome, so his see is the see of Rome, which Catholics call the Holy See, or the Apostolic See. What does the name cover?
The Code of Canon Law says it means the pope himself, and also the offices that help him govern the Church, like the Secretariat of State.
So when the Holy See signs an agreement or sends a nuncio abroad, it's the pope's office acting, not a city. Why give this see its weight?

Catholics point to Jesus's words to Peter in Matthew's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "And I say to thee: That thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it."
Catholic tradition holds that Peter's ministry continues in the bishops of Rome, where Peter died.
Orthodox Christians honor the bishop of Rome in their own way, and Protestant churches read the verse in other ways; the Catholic reading is the one this path follows.
Vatican City is a small sovereign territory, and its point is protection: a pope who answered to a government could be pressured by it.
The state is the shell; the see is what it carries, like a backpack and the letter inside it.

how: Catholics pray for the pope by name in the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass, and some pray for the pope's intentions, often with an Our Father and a Hail Mary. Nations send ambassadors to the Holy See, and the Holy See sends nuncios to them.

games.q: you're a new ambassador sent to Rome to represent your country to the pope. whose name goes on your papers?
games.why: ambassadors are accredited to the Holy See, the pope's office, not to the small state that protects it.

practice: Think of how much passes across one desk in a single day: letters from bishops, news of wars and floods, decisions about people far away.
If you pray, pray for the pope and those who work alongside him; some Catholics pray an Our Father and a Hail Mary for the pope's intentions, or simply hold him in silence.
If you don't pray, hold in mind anyone who carries heavy decisions for many people, and wish them wisdom.

wordCard.voice: The Holy See. The pope's office as bishop of Rome, with the offices that serve him, protected by a small state. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, the Holy See: literally the holy seat.
